name: Barriere to the prince of Conde, London 20 Nov 1654 N.S. (Birch, Thurloe State Papers vol.2 pp.721-722)
ciphertext: ciphers/thurloe-barriere-1654/ciphertext.tsv (YX-BARB, 25 Sept 2026: passA.tsv, TX-BARRT's single eye transcription, reconciled against passB.tsv, a second blind Sonnet pass, and settled from the page images -- 33 runs, 400 tokens; see NOTES.md 'YX-BARB' section. passA.tsv/passB.tsv kept for provenance.)
alphabet: 1-2 digit numerals (mostly 4-99) plus a small set of italic single-letter codes (a b c d e f m o p r u x, and the doubled 'll') and two astrological/planetary-looking symbols, embedded inline within otherwise plain French prose (a nomenclature/code-word system, not a full-text substitution); roughly half the numeral tokens carry a diacritic-like mark printed directly above them (circumflex, grave, acute, macron/overline, caron, diaeresis) whose exact type this pass could not reliably distinguish at the available resolution -- mark presence only is recorded (passA.tsv trailing '*'), not type
constraints: design is word-per-code nomenclature, not letter substitution: two spans give an exact word-count match between a fully-printed interlinear gloss phrase and the run's token count (19 tokens / 19 words; 7 tokens / 7 words -- see NOTES.md s.2), read in sequential order (typesetting does not column-align gloss words under their source token)

the gloss is sparse and partial: of 42 runs (368 code tokens total, this pass's count) only 25 runs have any printed gloss at all, and most of those reveal only the first few words of the run, not the whole thing

heavy homophone/conflict structure: the same bare digit recurs with DIFFERENT gloss-derived values at different confidently-glossed spots for at least 9 codes (61, 12, 40, 44, 88, 90, 89, 31, d -- see key_gloss.tsv 'conflict' rows), consistent with a nomenclature that gives its most frequent short words (le/la/que/ne/de/se) many interchangeable code slots specifically to defeat frequency attack -- this pass's 'primary' key uses only the 30 codes that showed no such conflict

no full key or prior decipherment of this letter is known (check-solved: open, see NOTES.md; the correspondence's separate 1655 cipher noted in the solver repositories is a different key per TX-BARR's inventory)
cheap_tests_in_order: apply the gloss-derived 'primary' (non-conflicting) key to every run in the letter and measure coverage, then compare against a matched control of the same design (word-per-code nomenclature, same 42-run/368-token structure, same per-run gloss-reveal counts, homophone conflicts, built over fresh unrelated period French instead of the target's own words) -- TX-BARRT, 25 Sept 2026, done, see cheap_test_done below

a permutation z-test (key-shuffle null and token-shuffle null) on the letter's own real gloss positions, leave-one-out: is a held-out gloss occurrence of a code predictable from that code's OTHER gloss occurrences, more than chance? -- ZX-BAR, 25 Sept 2026, done, see cheap_test_done[1] below
